title.zh: 卷九 帝紀第九 太宗簡文帝 孝武帝
title.en: Volume 9 Annals 9: Emperor Jianwen; Emperor Xiaowu
title.raw: 卷九 帝紀第九 太宗簡文帝 孝武帝 Volume 9 Annals 9: Emperor Jianwen; Emperor Xiaowu

sentences.zh: 簡文帝

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen

sentences.zh: 簡文皇帝諱昱，字道萬，元帝之少子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwens taboo name was Yu; his courtesy name was Daowan; he was the youngest son of Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen was born Yu, styled Daowan, the youngest son of Emperor Yuan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 幼而岐嶷，爲元帝所愛。

translations.literal: In childhood he was precocious and was loved by Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed unusual alertness, and Emperor Yuan doted on him.

sentences.zh: 郭璞見而謂人曰：「興晉祚者，必此人也。

translations.literal: Guo Pu saw him and said to people: “The one who will raise up the fortunes of Jin must be this person.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu looked at him and told others that this boy would be the one to restore Jin’s fortunes.

sentences.zh: 」及長，清虛寡欲，尤善玄言。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was pure and empty [of desire], with few wants, and was especially good at “Dark Learning” discourse.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he cultivated clarity of mind and few desires, and excelled at philosophical conversation in the xuanxue manner.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，元帝詔曰：「先公武王、先考恭王君臨琅邪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang [322 CE], Emperor Yuan issued an edict saying: “My late father King Wu and my late father King Gong ruled Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang 1, Yuan issued an edict: “My grandfather King Wu of Langye and my father King Gong held sway there.

sentences.zh: 繼世相承，國嗣未立，蒸嘗靡主，朕常悼心。

translations.literal: Succession continued generation after generation, yet the heir of the state has not been established; there is no master for the seasonal sacrifices at the ancestral temple, and I constantly mourn in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The succession passed down through generations, but no heir had yet been named for the kingdom’s shrine—there was no one to tend the offerings—and this weighed on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 子昱仁明有智度，可以虔奉宗廟，以慰罔極之恩。

translations.literal: The son Yu is humane and wise and possesses judgment; he can reverently serve the ancestral temples and comfort the boundless kindness [shown me].
translations.idiomatic: Yu is humane, discerning, and fit to honor the shrines and repay grace beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 其封昱爲琅邪王，食會稽、宣城如舊。

translations.literal: Therefore enfeoff Yu as Prince of Langye, with Kuaiji and Xuancheng as his provisions as before.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yu enfeoffed as Prince of Langye, with Kuaiji and Xuancheng as before.

sentences.zh: 」咸和元年，所生鄭夫人薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianhe [326 CE], Lady Zheng, his birth mother, died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe 1 his natural mother, Lady Zheng, died.

sentences.zh: 帝時年七歲，號慕泣血，固請服重。

translations.literal: The emperor was then seven years old; he wailed in longing until blood came from his tears, and firmly requested heavy mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: He was only seven but mourned so intensely he wept blood and insisted on observing full mourning.

sentences.zh: 成帝哀而許之，故徙封會稽王，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng pitied him and granted it; therefore [Yu’s] fief was transferred and he became Prince of Kuaiji, and he was appointed Palace Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng relented: Yu’s seat moved to Prince of Kuaiji and he received the post of supernumerary gentleman attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷右將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year [335 CE], he was promoted to General of the Right and given concurrent status as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he rose to General of the Right with concurrent palace attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 咸康六年，進撫軍將軍，領秘書監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiankang [340 CE], he was advanced to General Who Guards the Army and took charge of the Secretariat Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang 6 brought promotion to General Who Guards the Army with supervision of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 建元元年夏五月癸丑，康帝詔曰：「太常職奉天地，兼掌宗廟，其爲任也，可謂重矣。

translations.literal: In summer, fifth month, guichou day [June 8], first year of Jianyuan [343 CE], Emperor Kang issued an edict: “The office of Chamberlain for Ceremonials serves Heaven and Earth and also oversees the ancestral temple; its burden may truly be called heavy.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the fifth month of summer, Jianyuan 1, Kang declared that the Grand Master of Ceremonies tended Heaven and Earth and the imperial shrines—a weighty charge.

sentences.zh: 是以古今選建，未嘗不妙簡時望，兼之儒雅。

translations.literal: Therefore whether ancient or modern in selecting and establishing [someone for it], none has ever failed to carefully choose from the eminent worthies of the age and add men of refined Confucian culture.
translations.idiomatic: Across ages appointees were drawn carefully from leading scholar-officials renowned for learning.

sentences.zh: 會稽王叔履尚清虛，志道無倦，優遊上列，諷議朝肆。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Kuaiji, my uncle, walks [his path] honoring purity and emptiness; his mind is set on the Way without weariness; he moves at ease among the highest ranks and offers measured criticism in court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: The prince uncle of Kuaiji keeps to purity and few desires, tires never of the Way, moves easily among the elite, and weighs policy in court debate.

sentences.zh: 其領太常本官如故。

translations.literal: Let him continue as Chamberlain for Ceremonials with his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was to keep his chamberlain title alongside existing duties.

sentences.zh: 」永和元年，崇德太后臨朝，進位撫軍大將軍、錄尚書六條事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghe [345 CE], Empress Dowager Chongde held court from behind the curtain; [Yu] was promoted to Grand General Who Guards the Army and Recorder of Affairs with regard to the Six Articles.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe 1: with Chongde regency he rose to Grand General Who Guards the Army and recorder of affairs for the six statutes.

sentences.zh: 二年，驃騎何充卒，崇德太后詔帝專總萬機。

translations.literal: In the second year [346 CE], He Chong, General-in-Chief Who Inspires Might, died; Empress Dowager Chongde issued an edict that the emperor alone assume overall direction of the myriad tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Next year He Chong died; the empress dowager ordered sole custody of government for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 八年，進位司徒，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year [352 CE], he was promoted to Minister of Education but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Year eight: minister of education—he repeatedly refused.

sentences.zh: 穆帝始冠，帝稽首歸政，不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu came of age [at the capping ceremony], the emperor bowed prostrate and returned the government, but [his petition] was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: At Mu’s capping he sought to yield power; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 廢帝卽位，以琅邪王絕嗣，復徙封琅邪，而封王子昌明爲會稽王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yi succeeded to the throne, because the Prince of Langye had no heir, [Yu] was again transferred to Langye’s title, while his son Changming was enfeoffed Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yi (the future Duke of Haixi) ascended, the Langye title still needed an occupant, so Yu resumed it while his son Changming received Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 帝固讓，故雖封琅邪而不去會稽之號。

translations.literal: The emperor firmly declined; therefore although he was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye he did not relinquish the designation “Prince of Kuaiji.”
translations.idiomatic: He resisted losing Kuaiji—Langye was added but he kept calling himself prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，進位丞相、錄尚書事，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿，給羽葆鼓吹班劍六十人，又固讓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe [366 CE], he was promoted to Chancellor and Recorder of Affairs; he entered court without hurrying, needed not name himself when praised at audience, could wear sword and shoes on the hall, was granted feather-canopy imperial drums and “pattern sword” escort of sixty men—and again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 1 piled honors—chancellor, recorder, imperial etiquette—and again he refused.

sentences.zh: 及廢帝廢，皇太后詔曰：「丞相、錄尚書、會稽王體自中宗，明德劭令，英秀玄虛，神棲事外。

translations.literal: When the Haixi duke was deposed, the empress dowager issued an edict: “The Chancellor, Recorder of Affairs, Prince of Kuaiji issued from Middle Ancestor [Yuan]; his bright virtue was lofty and his commands admirable; he was gifted and refined in “Dark” subtlety; his spirit lodged beyond mundane affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Her edict praised the prince’s Yuan ancestry, virtue, and withdrawn temperament.

sentences.zh: 以具瞻允塞，故阿衡三世。

translations.literal: Because of “holding up all eyes” and filling every expectation, therefore he has aided [regency over] three reigns.
translations.idiomatic: All quarters looked to him; he had steadied three sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 道化宣流，人望攸歸，爲日已久。

translations.literal: His transforming influence spread abroad; the peoples hopes turned to him; this has long been so.
translations.idiomatic: His moral sway was entrenched; popularity favored him for years.

sentences.zh: 宜從天人之心，以統皇極。

translations.literal: He ought to follow the hearts of Heaven and man and take up the supreme pinnacle.
translations.idiomatic: He should ascend by universal acclaim.

sentences.zh: 主者明依舊典，以時施行。

translations.literal: Let those in charge clarify according to the old statutes and implement them in due course.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were told to follow precedent and act promptly.

sentences.zh: 」于是大司馬桓溫率百官進太極前殿，具乘輿法駕，奉迎帝于會稽邸，于朝堂變服，著平巾幘單衣，東向拜受璽綬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Marshal Huan Wen led the hundred officials into the Hall before the Supreme Ultimate; they prepared the imperial carriage and regalia and welcomed the emperor from his Kuaiji residence; in the court hall they changed dress; wearing plain headcloth and single garment he faced east, bowed, and received the seal-cords.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen ushered the court to Taiji Hall with full panoply and fetched Yu from Kuaiji; Yu changed clothes, faced east in humble dress, and took the seals.

sentences.zh: 戊午，詔曰：「王室多故，穆哀早世，皇胤夙遷，神器無主。

translations.literal: On wuwu day [July 7], an edict stated: “The royal house has suffered many troubles; Mu and Ai died young; the imperial heir shifted prematurely; the sacred vessel lacked a master.
translations.idiomatic: His first edict (wuwu): turmoil had orphaned the throne—Mu and Ai gone young, succession unstable.

sentences.zh: 東海王以母弟近屬，入纂大統，嗣位經年，昏闇亂常，人倫虧喪，大禍將及，則我祖宗之靈靡知所託。

translations.literal: The Prince of the Eastern Sea, as a uterine younger brother and close kinsman, entered to inherit the great lineage; he had been on the throne for a year but was dark and deranged, overturned constant norms, and human relations were ruined—great disaster would arrive—then the spirits of our ancestors would have nowhere to rely.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yi had seemed a plausible heir as a close prince, yet within a year his misrule threatened the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 皇太后深懼皇基，時定大計。

translations.literal: The empress dowager deeply feared for the dynastic foundation and at that time settled the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: The regent feared for the realm and fixed succession.

sentences.zh: 大司馬因順天人，協同神略，親帥羣后，恭承明命。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, complying with Heaven and men and harmonizing with divine strategy, personally led the hosts of nobles and reverently received the enlightened mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen acted with Heaven’s mandate and led lords to obey.

sentences.zh: 雲霧旣除，皇極載清，乃顧朕躬，仰承弘緒。

translations.literal: Once the clouds and fog were cleared away and the supreme pinnacle was restored to purity, then they looked to my humble person to uphold the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: With chaos lifted they installed Yu—the speaker claims humility.

sentences.zh: 雖伊尹之寧殷朝，博陸之安漢室，無以尚也。

translations.literal: Even Yi Yin’s settling of the Yin court or Boling’s stabilizing of Han could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Not even Yi Yin or Huo Guang surpassed such steadiness.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡德，猥居元首，實懼眇然，不克負荷，戰戰兢兢，罔知攸濟。

translations.literal: I, with scant virtue, basely occupy the position of chief; I truly fear my insignificance and cannot bear the burden—trembling with anxiety I do not know how to cross.
translations.idiomatic: The voice admits weak virtue and dread of the throne.

sentences.zh: 思與兆庶更始，其大赦天下，大酺五日，增文武位二等，孝順忠貞鰥寡孤獨米人五斛。

translations.literal: I wish together with the myriad common people to make a fresh beginning; therefore greatly pardon all under Heaven; hold grand communal drinking for five days; advance civil and military ranks two grades; give grain five hu per household to the filial, obedient, loyal, chaste, widowers, orphans, and solitary elderlies.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed amnesty, five days of public feast, rank bonuses, and grain relief.

sentences.zh: 」己未，賜溫軍三萬人，人布一匹，米一斛。

translations.literal: On jiwei day [July 8], [the court] granted three myriad troops to [Huan] Wen—each man one bolt of cloth and one hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Wen’s army received cloth and grain allotments.

sentences.zh: 庚申，加大司馬桓溫爲丞相，不受。

translations.literal: On gengshen [July 9], Grand Marshal Huan Wen was advanced to Chancellor—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was offered chancellor; he declined.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，溫旋自白石，因鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: On xinyou [July 10], Wen returned from Baishi and then stationed at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew from Baishi and camped at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 以冠軍將軍毛武生都督荊州之沔中、揚州之義城諸軍事。

translations.literal: Champion General Mao Wusheng was made Area Commander-in-Chief for Hannan in Jingzhou and Yicheng in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Wusheng took river-defense commands across Jing and Yang sectors.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊子，詔以京都有經年之儲，權停一年之運。

translations.literal: In twelfth month, wuzi day [Jan 9], because the capital had stores lasting years, transport levies were suspended for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Late year: grain surplus paused tribute convoys for one cycle.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，廢東海王奕爲海西公，食邑四千戶。

translations.literal: On gengyin [Jan 11], Prince Yi of the Eastern Sea was demoted to Duke of Haixi with four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yi was reduced to Duke of Haixi with a token fief.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，初薦酃淥酒於太廟。

translations.literal: On xinmao [Jan 12], Linglu wine from Ling county was first offered in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time Ling spirits blessed the temple altar.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛丑，百濟、林邑王各遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, xinchou day [Feb 10]: Baekje and the king of Linyi each sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje and Champa envoys arrived with gifts.

sentences.zh: 二月，苻堅伐慕容桓于遼東，滅之。

translations.literal: In second month Fu Jian attacked Murong Huan in Liaodong and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin crushed Murong Huan in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉，詔曰：「朕居阿衡三世，不能濟彼時雍，乃至海西失德，殆傾皇祚。

translations.literal: Third month, dingyou day [Apr 9], an edict stated: “I have occupied the office that aids [the throne] through three reigns yet could not bring timely harmony; indeed Haixi lost virtue and nearly overturned the imperial altar.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyou edict: regret over weak governance before the Haixi disaster.

sentences.zh: 賴祖宗靈祗之德，皇太后淑體應期，籓輔忠賢，百官戮力，用能蕩氣務於昊蒼，耀晨輝於宇宙。

translations.literal: Relying on the virtue of our ancestral spirits and numinous powers and the empress dowagers timely virtue answering heaven; with loyal worthy governors at the screen and the hundred officials striving together—thus could we wash away ill vapors toward broad Heaven and let mornings brilliance shine through the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks ancestors and officials order returned.

sentences.zh: 遂以眇身，托于王公之上，思賴羣賢，以弼其闕。

translations.literal: Therefore upon my insignificant person [they] relied to mount above the kings and dukes—I hope to rely on the crowd of worthies to remedy my shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: He appeals to ministers to shore his faults.

sentences.zh: 夫敦本息末，抑絕華競，使清濁異流，能否殊貫，官無秕政，士無謗讟，不有懲勸，則德禮焉施？

translations.literal: For settling foundation and restraining branch ends, suppressing and cutting off vain rivalry, making clear and turbid flow apart and competence and incompetence wear distinct cords—if officials lack spoiled governance and gentlemen lack slanderous gossip, without punishment and encouragement how could virtue and ritual be applied?
translations.idiomatic: He urges sorting talent and thrift—without incentives virtue fails.

sentences.zh: 且強寇未殄，勞役未息，自非軍國戎祀之耍，其華飾煩費之用皆省之。

translations.literal: Moreover the strong foe is not yet extinguished and corvée labor has not ceased—unless it be essential for army, state, or martial sacrifice, all lavish ornament and burdensome expense shall be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: War continues—cut court luxury outside military or ritual need.

sentences.zh: 夫肥遁窮穀之賢，滑泥揚波之士，雖抗志玄霄，潛默幽岫，貪屈高尚之道，以隆協贊之美，孰與自足山水，棲遲丘壑，徇匹夫之潔，而忘兼濟之大邪？

translations.literal: As for worthies who hide in deep valleys or scholars who slide through mud yet lift waves—even though they oppose their aspirations to the dark heavens and silently dwell in remote ravines—coveting lofty withdrawal yet wishing to elevate cooperative assistance—which compares with sufficing oneself with mountains and waters, lingering on hills and gullies, pursuing a common mans purity while forgetting the greater good of aiding all?
translations.idiomatic: He summons recluses who spurn office yet could serve the state.

sentences.zh: 古人不借賢於曩代，朕所以虛想於今日。

translations.literal: The ancients did not begrudge worthies from former ages; that is why I vainly long for them today.
translations.idiomatic: Past courts used talent; he seeks the same now.

sentences.zh: 內外百官，各勤所司，使善無不達，惡無不聞，令詩人元素餐之刺，而吾獲虛心之求焉。」

translations.literal: Let civil and military officials inside and outside each exert their duties so that good never goes unheard and evil never goes unseen—make the poets complaint about “white rice without labor” disappear and give me the gain of an empty heart seeking [truth].
translations.idiomatic: Demand diligence so laziness vanishes.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔曰：「吾承祖宗洪基，而昧于政道，懼不能允厘天工，克隆先業，夕惕惟憂，若涉泉冰。

translations.literal: On guichou day [Apr 25], an edict stated: “I inherit the vast foundation of ancestors yet am dark about the way of government; I fear I cannot harmoniously regulate Heaven’s works or enlarge the prior enterprise—night and day anxious as if treading spring ice.
translations.idiomatic: Guichou self-reproach: fear of misrule.

sentences.zh: 賴宰輔忠德，道濟伊望，羣后竭誠，協契斷金，內外盡匡翼之規，文武致匪躬之節，冀因斯道，終克弘濟。

translations.literal: Relying on the prime ministers loyal virtue—his conduct matches Yi Yin and Lü Wang; the hosts of lords exhaust sincerity; [the realm is] solid as alloyed metal; inside and outside exhaust rules of support; civil and military show utmost devotion—I hope by this way ultimately to achieve great relief.
translations.idiomatic: He credited his chief minister with Yi Yin–level steadiness and complete court loyalty.

sentences.zh: 每念干戈未戢，公私疲悴，籓鎮有疆理之務，征戍懷《東山》之勤，或白首戎陣，忠勞未敘，或行役彌久，擔石靡儲，何嘗不昧旦晨興，夜分忘寢。

translations.literal: Each time I think that weapons of war are not yet laid away and public and private are worn out—screen princes have duties of guarding borders; garrison troops cherish the toil of “East Mountain”—some grow old in camp yet loyalty goes unrewarded; some serve endlessly yet lack even a peck of stored grain—how could I not rise before dawn and forget sleep at midnight?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers suffer—he shares their burden emotionally.

sentences.zh: 雖未能撫而巡之，且欲達其此心。

translations.literal: Although I cannot yet go to comfort and inspect them, I wish at least to convey this heart.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot tour armies but would signal concern.

sentences.zh: 可遣大使詣大司馬，幷問方伯，逮于邊戍，宣詔大饗，求其所安。

translations.literal: Dispatch great envoys to the Grand Marshal and jointly inquire of regional shepherds down to border garrisons—proclaim edicts for grand feasts and learn what would settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys will feast troops and ask needs.

sentences.zh: 又籌量賜給，悉令周普。」

translations.literal: Further calculate grants and give aid so all receive thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Calculate stipends fairly.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔曰：「往事故之後，百度未充，羣僚常俸，並皆寡約，蓋隨時之義也。

translations.literal: On yimao day [Apr 27], an edict stated: “After past incidents the hundred measures were not yet sufficient; the regular salaries of the host of officials were all meager—this was the propriety of following the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yimao: post-crisis salaries were thin by necessity.

sentences.zh: 然退食在朝，而祿不代耕，非經通之制。

translations.literal: Yet leaving court after the meal [official life] while salary does not substitute for farming is not a thorough norm.
translations.idiomatic: Court pay still failed to equal farming income.

sentences.zh: 今資儲漸豐，可籌量增俸。

translations.literal: Now stores gradually abound; one may calculate and increase salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries improved—raise official pay.

sentences.zh: 」騶虞見豫章。

translations.literal: The zouyu [auspicious beast] appeared in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: A zouyu was sighted in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，徙海西公於吳縣西柴里。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, the Duke of Haixi was moved to Chaili west of Wu county.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed ruler was sent west of Wu county to Chaili.

sentences.zh: 追貶庾后曰夫人。

translations.literal: Posthumously demoted Empress Yu to “Lady.”
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yu was posthumously stripped to Lady.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使拜百濟王餘句爲鎮東將軍，領樂浪太守。

translations.literal: In sixth month envoys invested King Gouyu of Baekje as General Who Guards the East with concurrent office as prefect of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje’s king got eastern command and Lelang title.

sentences.zh: 戊子，前護軍將軍庾希舉兵反，自海陵入京口，晉陵太守卞眈奔于曲阿。

translations.literal: On wuzi day [Aug 2], former General Who Guards the Army Yu Xi raised troops in rebellion, entering from Hailing; Jinling prefect Bian Dan fled to Qu’a.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi rebelled from Hailing; the prefect fled.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬辰，桓溫遣東海內史周少孫討希，擒之，斬于建康市。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, renchen day [Sept 3]: Huan Wen sent Administrator of the Eastern Seas Zhou Shaosun to campaign against Xi, captured him, and executed him in the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: Huan’s force caught Yu Xi and executed him publicly.

sentences.zh: 己未，立會稽王昌明爲皇太子，皇子道子爲琅邪王，領會稽內史。

translations.literal: On jiwei day [Sept 30], Prince Changming of Kuaiji was established as crown prince; the imperial son Daozi was made Prince of Langye with concurrent office as interior steward of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince Changming; Daozi to Langye with Kuaiji interior administration.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝崩于東堂，時年五十三。

translations.literal: That same day the emperor died in the Eastern Hall; he was fifty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died that evening in the Eastern Hall at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 葬高平陵，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: He was buried at Gaoping Mausoleum; his temple name was Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Burial at Gaoping; temple Taizong.

sentences.zh: 遺詔以桓溫輔政，依諸葛亮、王導故事。

translations.literal: His testamentary edict named Huan Wen to assist the government, following the precedent of Zhuge Liang and Wang Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Will entrusted regency to Huan Wen like Zhuge Liang or Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 帝少有風儀，善容止，留心典籍，不以居處爲意，凝塵滿席，湛如也。

translations.literal: In youth he had bearing and grace; he was skilled in deportment; he applied his mind to classical writings and did not care about his dwelling—dust filled his mat yet he remained tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Youth: dignified, bookish, indifferent to housekeeping—dust on the seat yet calm.

sentences.zh: 嘗與桓溫及武陵王晞同載遊版橋，溫遽令鳴鼓吹角，車馳卒奔，欲觀其所爲。

translations.literal: Once he rode with Huan Wen and Prince Xi of Wuling to Ban Bridge on an outing; Wen suddenly ordered drums and horns sounded and chariots and runners to gallop, wishing to observe what he would do.
translations.idiomatic: Huan tested him with sudden martial noise on an outing.

sentences.zh: 晞大恐，求下車，而帝安然無懼色，溫由此憚服。

translations.literal: Xi was greatly frightened and begged to leave the carriage, yet the emperor remained calm without fear—thereupon Wen feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi panicked; Yu stayed composed—Huan respected him.

sentences.zh: 溫旣仗文武之任，屢建大功，加以廢立，威振內外。

translations.literal: Once Wen relied on civil and military responsibilities and repeatedly achieved great merit, further adding deposition and enthronement—his awesomeness shook inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Huan’s power grew through victories and coups.

sentences.zh: 帝雖處尊位，拱默守道而已，常懼廢黜。

translations.literal: Although the emperor occupied the honored position, he folded his hands in silence and guarded the Way only—he constantly feared deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Yu kept quiet on the throne, fearing removal.

sentences.zh: 先是，熒惑入太微，尋而海西廢。

translations.literal: Before this, Mars entered the Forbidden Enclosure; soon Haixi was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The same omen had preceded the Duke of Haixi’s removal.

sentences.zh: 及帝登阼，熒惑又入太微，帝甚惡焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne Mars again entered the Forbidden Enclosure; the emperor greatly loathed it.
translations.idiomatic: It recurred at his accession—ominous to him.

sentences.zh: 時中書郎郗超在直，帝乃引入，謂曰：「命之修短，本所不計，故當無復近日事邪！

translations.literal: At that time Palace Secretary Xi Chao was on duty; the emperor summoned him in and said: “As for length or brevity of fate, fundamentally I do not calculate—so surely there will not again be recent matters like those!
translations.idiomatic: He asked Xi Chao whether short rule meant another coup.

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「大司馬臣溫方內固社稷，外恢經略，非常之事，臣以百口保之。

translations.literal: Xi replied: “The Grand Marshal, minister Wen, is at present securing the altars within and expanding strategy without—as for extraordinary matters, your servant pledges his hundred kin upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi assured him Huan Wen was securing home and frontier—no coup imminent.

sentences.zh: 」及超請急省其父，帝謂之曰：「致意尊公，家國之事，遂至於此！

translations.literal: When Xi requested urgent leave to visit his father, the emperor said to him: “Convey my regards to your worthy father—affairs of house and state have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: When Xi left for his father, Yu lamented state disaster.

sentences.zh: 由吾不能以道匡衛，愧歎之深，言何能喻。

translations.literal: It is because I could not rectify and defend with the Way—how deeply I sigh with shame; how can words convey it?
translations.idiomatic: He blamed himself for failing moral guidance.

sentences.zh: 」因詠庾闡詩云「志士痛朝危，忠臣哀主辱」，遂泣下霑襟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recited Yu Kais verse “A resolute scholar grieves the mornings peril; a loyal minister sorrows the lords humiliation”—and tears fell soaking his lapel.
translations.idiomatic: He wept reciting loyalist poetry.

sentences.zh: 帝雖神識恬暢，而無濟世大略，故謝安稱爲惠帝之流，清談差勝耳。

translations.literal: Although the emperors spiritual knowing was peaceful and open, he lacked great strategies to aid the age—therefore Xie An called him of the same kind as Emperor Hui—pure conversation only rather better.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An likened him to Emperor Hui—better talker, no statesmanship.

sentences.zh: 沙門支道林嘗言「會稽有遠體而無遠神」。

translations.literal: The monk Zhi Dun once said: “Kuaiji has remote deportment but lacks remote spirit.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Dun quipped Kuaiji had manner without depth.

sentences.zh: 謝靈運迹其行事，亦以爲赧獻之輩云。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun traced his conduct and also considered him of the same sort as He Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun grouped him with idle talkers like He Yan.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝諱曜，字昌明，簡文帝第三子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowus taboo name was Yao; his courtesy name was Changming; he was the third son of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu was Yao, styled Changming, third son of Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 興寧三年七月甲申，初封會稽王。

translations.literal: In third year of Xingning [365 CE], seventh month, jiashen day [Aug 25], he was first enfeoffed Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xingning 3 jiashen: first enfeoffment as Kuaiji prince.

sentences.zh: 咸安二年秋七月己未，立爲皇太子。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, jiwei day [Sept 7], second year of Xian’an [372 CE], he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xian’an 2 jiwei: named heir.

sentences.zh: 是日，簡文帝崩，太子卽皇帝位。

translations.literal: That same day Emperor Jianwen died; the crown prince assumed the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Same day Jianwen died; he succeeded.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕以不造，奄丁閔凶，號天扣地。

translations.literal: An edict stated: “I, lacking [good] formation, suddenly encountered bitter mourning—I cry to Heaven and strike the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Edict opens with orphan’s grief at sudden death.

sentences.zh: 靡知所訴。

translations.literal: I do not know to whom to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: He had nowhere to turn in grief.

sentences.zh: 藐然幼沖，眇若綴旒，深惟社稷之重，大懼不克負荷。

translations.literal: I am tiny in infancy; I hang like a tassel streamer—I deeply ponder the weight of the altars and greatly fear I cannot bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Youth on the throne—fears carrying the realm.

sentences.zh: 仰憑祖宗之靈，積德之祀。

translations.literal: I look up and rely on the spirits of ancestors and the sacrifices of accumulated virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He invokes ancestral merit.

sentences.zh: 先帝淳風玄化，遺詠在民。

translations.literal: The late emperors pure wind and dark transforming influence—his lingering praise remains among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Late father’s legacy still praised among folk.

sentences.zh: 宰輔英賢，勳隆德盛。

translations.literal: The chief ministers are worthy and talented; their merit is lofty and their virtue abundant.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers combined eminent talent with towering merit and reputation.

sentences.zh: 顧命之託，實賴匡訓。

translations.literal: The charge delivered at the bedside truly relies on correction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary trust in them depended on their steering the young ruler.

sentences.zh: 羣后率職，百僚勤政。

translations.literal: The regional lords each fulfill their duties; the hundred officials diligently administer government.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial magnates kept their posts and the bureaucracy stayed at work.

sentences.zh: 冀孤弱之躬有寄，皇極之基不墜。

translations.literal: [I] hope my orphaned, weak person may find someone to rely on, and that the foundation of the supreme pinnacle may not fall.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed his youth would find support so the throne would not stumble.

sentences.zh: 先恩遺惠，播于四海，思弘餘潤，以康黎庶。

translations.literal: Prior kindness and lingering bounty spread within the four seas; [I] wish to extend the remaining moisture to bring peace to the black-haired multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to spread his father’s legacy and ease the common people’s hardship.

sentences.zh: 其大赦天下，與民更始。」

translations.literal: Therefore greatly pardon all under Heaven and give the people a fresh beginning.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a general amnesty and a new beginning for the realm.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅，追尊皇妣會稽王妃曰順皇后。

translations.literal: Ninth month, jiayin day [Oct 16, 372 CE]: posthumously honored his birth mother, consort of the Prince of Kuaiji, as Empress Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated his late mother, the Kuaiji consort, to Empress Shun.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁卯，葬簡文皇帝于高平陵。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, dingmao day [Nov 27]: Emperor Jianwen was buried at Gaoping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Late autumn brought Jianwen’s interment at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲午，妖賊盧悚晨入殿庭，遊擊將軍毛安之等討擒之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jiawu day [Jan 5, 373 CE]: the sorcerer-rebel Lu Song entered the palace courtyard at dawn; Mobile Corps General Mao Anzhi and others attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Song’s dawn raid on the hall ended when Mao Anzhi seized him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，三吳大旱，人多餓死，詔所在振給。

translations.literal: That year the Three Wu suffered severe drought; many people starved to death; an edict ordered relief wherever needed.
translations.idiomatic: Drought across Wu brought starvation; the court ordered local grain relief.

sentences.zh: 苻堅陷仇池，執秦州刺史楊世。

translations.literal: Fu Jian took Chouchi and seized Qinzhou Inspector Yang Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin absorbed Chouchi and captured Yang Shi.

sentences.zh: 寧康元年春正月己丑朔，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, jichou day [Feb 12, 373 CE], new moon of Ningkang 1: the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Ningkang opened with a new reign title on the jichou new moon.

sentences.zh: 二月，大司馬桓溫來朝。

translations.literal: Second month: Grand Marshal Huan Wen came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen entered the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 三月癸丑，詔除丹陽竹格等四桁稅。

translations.literal: Third month, guichou day [Apr 13]: an edict abolished the bamboo-barrier and related bridge tolls at four crossings in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: River-crossing tolls at four Danyang bridges were lifted.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，旱。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: drought.
translations.idiomatic: Midsummer drought returned.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、丞相、錄尚書、大司馬、揚州牧、平北將軍、徐兗二州刺史、南郡公桓溫薨。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, jihai day [Aug 23]: Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of all military affairs civil and foreign, Chancellor, Recorder of Affairs, Grand Marshal, Yangzhou shepherd, General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of Xu and Yan prefectures, Duke of Nanjun—Huan Wen—died.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen died laden with every civil and military title from Yangzhou shepherd to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，進右將軍桓豁爲征西將軍。

translations.literal: Gengxu day [Sep 3]: General of the Right Huan Huo was promoted to General Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Huo rose to western expedition command.

sentences.zh: 以江州刺史桓沖爲中軍將軍、都督揚豫江三州諸軍事、揚州刺史，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou Inspector Huan Chong was made General of the Central Army, commander-in-chief of Yang, Yu, and Jiang military affairs, Yangzhou shepherd, and stationed at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong took the central army, combined Yang-Yu-Jiang command, and camped at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 八月壬子，崇德太后臨朝攝政。

translations.literal: Eighth month, renzi day [Oct 15]: Empress Dowager Chongde faced court and acted as regent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager began her regency.

sentences.zh: 九月，苻堅將楊安寇成都。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Fu Jian’s general Yang An raided Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin pressed Chengdu under Yang An.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以尚書僕射王彪之爲尚書令，吏部尚書謝安爲尚書僕射，吳國內史刁彝爲北中郎將、徐兗二州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Bingshen day [Oct 22]: Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi became Director of the Secretariat; Minister of Personnel Xie An became Vice Director; Administrator of the Wu commandery Diao Yi became General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household and inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi headed the secretariat, Xie An became vice director, and Diao Yi held the northern Xu-Yan command at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 復置光祿勳、大司農、少府官。

translations.literal: The posts of Superintendent of the Imperial Household, Grand Minister of Agriculture, and Privy Treasurer were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Three palace finance offices were revived.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，西平公張天錫貢方物。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Duke of Xiping Zhang Tianxi presented local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Former Liang’s ruler sent tribute from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 十一月，苻堅將楊安陷梓潼及梁、益二州，刺史周仲孫帥騎五千南遁。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Fu Jian’s Yang An took Zitong and the Liang and Yi provinces; Inspector Zhou Zhongsun led five thousand horsemen south in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Yang An drove deep into Shu; Zhou Zhongsun quit his post with cavalry.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月癸未朔，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, guiwei day [Jan 27, 374 CE], new moon: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The second Ningkang year opened with a general pardon.

sentences.zh: 追封諡故會稽世子郁爲臨川獻王。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed and titled the former heir apparent of Kuaiji, Yu, as Prince Xian of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The late Kuaiji heir Yu received posthumous rank as Prince Xian of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 己酉，北中郎將、徐兗二州刺史刁彝卒。

translations.literal: Jiyou day [Feb 22]: General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household, inspector of Xu and Yan, Diao Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yi died in office on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 二月癸丑，以丹陽尹王坦之爲北中郎將、徐兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Second month, guichou day [Mar 28]: Governor of Danyang Wang Tanzhi became General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household and inspector of Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi replaced Diao Yi on the Xu-Yan line.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，有星孛于女虛。

translations.literal: Dingsi day [Apr 1]: a broom star appeared in the Girl and Emptiness asterisms.
translations.idiomatic: A comet trailed through Nü and Xu.

sentences.zh: 三月丙戌，彗星見於氐。

translations.literal: Third month, bingxu day [May 29]: a comet appeared in the Root asterism.
translations.idiomatic: A comet showed in the Dipper’s Root mansion.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬戌，皇太后詔曰：「頃玄象忒愆，上天表異，仰觀斯變，震懼于懷。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, renxu day [Jun 24]: the empress dowager issued an edict: “Recently celestial patterns have erred awry; High Heaven has displayed anomalies—looking up at these changes, [I] tremble in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: She blamed heaven’s omens for recent disasters.

sentences.zh: 夫因變致休，自古之道，朕敢不克意復心，以思厥中？

translations.literal: For turning anomaly into blessing is the way from antiquity—how dare I not constrain my intent and restore my heart, pondering what is balanced?
translations.idiomatic: She vowed reverent self-correction in the classical manner.

sentences.zh: 又三吳奧壤，股肱望郡，而水旱併臻，百姓失業，夙夜惟憂，不能忘懷，宜時拯卹，救其雕困。

translations.literal: Moreover the Three Wu are fertile heartland and arm-and-thigh commanderies, yet flood and drought arrived together; the hundred surnames lost their livelihoods—morning and night [I] worry only of this and cannot put it from mind—relief should be timely and rescue their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: She singled out Wu’s flooded counties for tax relief.

sentences.zh: 三吳義興、晉陵及會稽遭水之縣尤甚者，全除一年租布，其次聽除半年，受振貸者卽以賜之。」

translations.literal: For Yixing, Jinling, and Kuaiji counties worst hit by water in the Three Wu, completely remit one years rent and cloth; the next grade may remit half a year; households receiving relief grain shall count it as grant.
translations.idiomatic: Worst-hit counties received full or half-year rent waivers and forgiven loans.

sentences.zh: 五月，蜀人張育自號蜀王，帥衆圍成都，遣使稱籓。

translations.literal: Fifth month: the Shu man Zhang Yu styled himself King of Shu, led crowds besieging Chengdu, and sent envoys declaring submission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu proclaimed a Shu kingship and besieged Chengdu while offering Jin overlordship.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，涼州地震，山崩。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Liangzhou shook in an earthquake; mountains collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu quaked and slopes gave way.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將鄧羌攻張育，滅之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s Deng Qiang attacked Zhang Yu and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang crushed Zhang Yu for Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 八月，以長秋將建，權停婚姻。

translations.literal: Eighth month: because establishment of the empress was imminent, marriages were temporarily suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Weddings paused ahead of the empress investiture.

sentences.zh: 九月丁丑，有星孛于天市。

translations.literal: Ninth month, dingchou day [Oct 25]: a broom star appeared in the Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: A comet burned across the Celestial Market asterism.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月己酉，天門蜑賊攻郡，太守王匪死之，征西將軍桓豁遣師討平之。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, jiyou day [Dec 26]: Dan bandits at Tianmen attacked the commandery; Prefect Wang Fei died in the fighting; General Who Conquers the West Huan Huo sent troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Dan raiders killed Prefect Wang Fei until Huan Huo’s column restored order.

sentences.zh: 長城人錢步射、錢弘等作亂，吳興太守朱序討平之。

translations.literal: The Changcheng men Qian Bushe and Qian Hong raised rebellion; Administrator of Wuxing Zhu Xu attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Bushe’s rising in Changcheng fell to Zhu Xu.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，鎮遠將軍桓石虔破苻堅將姚萇於墊江。

translations.literal: Guiyou day [Jan 24, 375 CE]: General Who Guards the Distance Huan Shiqian defeated Fu Jian’s Yao Chang at Dianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shiqian broke Yao Chang’s army at Dianjiang.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月辛亥，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, xinhai day [Feb 18]: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Ningkang 3 began with empire-wide pardon.

sentences.zh: 夏五月丙午，北中郎將、徐兗二州刺史、藍田侯王坦之卒。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, bingwu day [Jun 21]: General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household, inspector of Xu and Yan, Marquis of Lantian Wang Tanzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi died holding the Xu-Yan frontier.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以中軍將軍、揚州刺史桓沖爲鎮北將軍、徐州刺史，鎮丹徒，尚書僕射謝安領揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Jiayin day [Jun 29]: General of the Central Army and Yangzhou shepherd Huan Chong became General Who Guards the North and Xuzhou inspector, stationed at Dantu; Vice Director of the Secretariat Xie An took Yangzhou shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong shifted north to Dantu while Xie An assumed Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋八月癸巳，立皇后王氏，大赦，加文武位一等。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, guisi day [Sep 13]: Empress Wang was established; great amnesty; civil and military ranks advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang’s installation came with amnesty and promotions.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝講《孝經》。

translations.literal: Ninth month: the emperor lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: He convened lectures on the Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, guiyou day [Nov 1], new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse darkened the tenth-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸未，神獸門災。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, guiwei day [Jan 18, 376 CE]: the Shenshou Gate burned.
translations.idiomatic: Fire destroyed the Shenshou Gate.

sentences.zh: 甲申，皇太后詔曰：「頃日蝕告變，水旱不適，雖克己思救，未盡其方。

translations.literal: Jiashen day [Jan 19]: the empress dowager issued an edict: “Recently a solar eclipse announced change; flood and drought were untimely—although [I] restrained myself and pondered rescue, [we] have not exhausted the methods.
translations.idiomatic: She tied eclipse and weather to imperfect governance.

sentences.zh: 其賜百姓窮者米，人五斛。

translations.literal: Therefore grant grain to destitute commoners—five hu per person.
translations.idiomatic: Five hu of grain went to the poorest households.

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，帝釋奠于中堂，祠孔子，以顏回配。

translations.literal: Guisi day [Jan 28]: the emperor performed the welcoming sacrifice in the Middle Hall, sacrificed to Confucius, with Yan Hui as correlate.
translations.idiomatic: He capped the observances with a Confucius offering in the middle hall.

sentences.zh: 太元元年春正月壬寅朔，帝加元服，見于太廟。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, renyin day [Feb 22, 376 CE], new moon of Taiyuan 1: the emperor received the capping regalia and appeared in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan opened with his majority rites at the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 皇太后歸政。

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned the government.
translations.idiomatic: The regency ended with her yielding power.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Jiachen day [Feb 24]: great amnesty; era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later came amnesty and the Taiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 丙午，帝始臨朝。

translations.literal: Bingwu day [Feb 26]: the emperor began holding court in person.
translations.idiomatic: He took personal direction of audiences.

sentences.zh: 以征西將軍桓豁爲征西大將軍，領軍將軍郗愔爲鎮軍大將軍，中軍將軍桓沖爲車騎將軍，加尚書僕射謝安中書監、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Huan Huo became Grand General Who Conquers the West; General Who Leads the Army Xi Yin became Grand General Who Guards the Army; General of the Central Army Huan Chong became General of Chariots and Cavalry; Vice Director Xie An added Palace Secretariat Supervisor and Recorder of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Huo, Xi Yin, Huan Chong, and Xie An were reshuffled at the summit of command.

sentences.zh: 甲子，謁建平等四陵。

translations.literal: Jiazi day [Mar 16]: [the emperor] visited the four tombs including Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He toured four imperial tombs beginning with Jianping.

sentences.zh: 夏五月癸丑，地震。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, guichou day [Jun 30]: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Summer brought another tremor.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔曰：「頃者上天垂監，譴告屢彰，朕有懼焉，震惕于心。

translations.literal: Jiayin day [Jul 1]: an edict stated: “Recently High Heaven lowered oversight—warnings have repeatedly appeared—I am fearful; my heart trembles.
translations.idiomatic: He read repeated omens as heaven’s rebuke.

sentences.zh: 思所以議獄緩死，赦過宥罪，庶因大變，與之更始。

translations.literal: Therefore ponder delaying executions in doubtful cases, pardoning faults and forgiving crimes—perhaps by means of the great change [we may] give them a fresh beginning.
translations.idiomatic: He sought clemency and reform through amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」于是大赦，增文武位各一等。

translations.literal: Thereupon there was a great amnesty; civil and military ranks each advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty followed, with another rank bonus.

sentences.zh: 六月，封河間王欽子範之爲章武王。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Fan Zhi, son of Prince of Hejian Quan, was enfeoffed Prince of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: A cadet branch of the imperial clan received the Zhangwu seat.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，苻堅將苟萇陷涼州，虜刺史張天錫，盡有其地。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Fu Jian’s Gou Chang took Liangzhou, captured Inspector Zhang Tianxi, and seized all its territory.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin extinguished Former Liang and took Zhang Tianxi captive.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，除度田收租之制，公王以下口稅米三斛，蠲在役之身。

translations.literal: Yisi day [Sep 9]: the land-measure rent system was abolished; from imperial princes downward each person owed three hu of grain tax; those currently serving labor were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced field-based rent with a flat per-capita rice levy and freed corvée bodies.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，移准北流人於淮南。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: refugees north of the Huai were resettled south of it.
translations.idiomatic: Huai frontier evacuees were moved into Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 十一月己巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jisi day [Dec 7], new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh-month sky showed an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔太官撤膳。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Imperial Catering to withdraw palace meals.
translations.idiomatic: Court kitchens cut royal fare as penance.

sentences.zh: 十二月，苻堅使其將苻洛攻代，執代王涉翼犍。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Fu Jian sent Fu Luo to attack Dai and seized Dai king Sheyi Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin struck Dai and captured the Tuoba ruler.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，繼絕世，紹功臣。

translations.literal: Spring, first month of year 2 [376 CE]: continued extinct noble lines and renewed merit households.
translations.idiomatic: He restored fallen titles and rewarded old service.

sentences.zh: 三月，以兗州刺史朱序爲南中郎將、梁州刺史、監沔中諸軍，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Third month: Yanzhou Inspector Zhu Xu became General of the Gentlemen of the South of the Center, Liangzhou inspector, and supervised Hannan military affairs, stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu took the Liang-Xiangyang theater.

sentences.zh: 閏月壬午，地震。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, renwu day [May 19]: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: An intercalary-month tremor shook the capital region.

sentences.zh: 甲申，暴風，折木髮屋。

translations.literal: Jiashen day [May 21]: violent wind snapped trees and tore off roofs.
translations.idiomatic: Gales ripped tiles and broke timber.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己酉，雨雹。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, jiyou day [Jun 22]: hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: Hail battered the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 五月丁丑，地震。

translations.literal: Fifth month, dingchou day [Jul 22]: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Earth shook again in summer.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，暴風，揚沙石。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jisi day [Aug 13]: violent wind drove sand and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Sandstorms scourged the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 林邑貢方物。

translations.literal: Linyi presented local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Champa sent envoys with gifts.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙卯，老人星見。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, yimao day [Aug 29]: the Old Man star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious Old Man star rose.

sentences.zh: 八月壬辰，四騎將軍桓沖來朝。

translations.literal: Eighth month, renchen day [Sep 25]: General of Chariots and Cavalry Huan Chong came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong rode to Jiankang for audience.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以尚書僕射謝安爲司徒。

translations.literal: Dingwei day [Oct 10]: Vice Director of the Secretariat Xie An became Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An stepped up to minister of education.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，使持節、都督荊梁寧益交廣六州諸軍事、荊州刺史、征西大將軍桓豁卒。

translations.literal: Bingchen day [Oct 19]: Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, commander-in-chief of Jing, Liang, Ning, Yi, Jiao, and Guang military affairs, Jingzhou inspector, Grand General Who Conquers the West Huan Huo died.
translations.idiomatic: The western pillar Huan Huo died in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛丑，以車騎將軍桓沖都督荊江梁益寧交廣七州諸軍事、領護南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，尚書王蘊爲徐州刺史、督江南晉陵諸軍，征西司馬謝玄爲兗州刺史、廣陵相、監江北諸軍。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, xinchou day [Nov 21]: General of Chariots and Cavalry Huan Chong became commander-in-chief of Jing, Jiang, Liang, Yi, Ning, Jiao, and Guang military affairs, Colonel of Southern Man and inspector of Jingzhou; Wang Yun became Xuzhou inspector commanding Jiangnan and Jinling forces; Western Expedition Major Xie Xuan became Yanzhou inspector, Guangling administrator, and supervised north-of-the-river military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong inherited the vast western command; Wang Yun and Xie Xuan took Xu and Yan-Yang respectively.

sentences.zh: 壬寅。

translations.literal: Renyin day [Nov 22].
translations.idiomatic: The chronicle notes the renyin day alone.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、左光祿大夫、尚書令王彪之卒。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance, Left Household Grandee, Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi, keeper of the secretariat, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚寅，以尚書王劭爲尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, gengyin day [Jan 15, 378 CE]: Director Wang Shao became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao succeeded at vice director.

sentences.zh: 三年春二月乙巳，作新宮，帝移居會稽王邸。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, yisi day [Mar 15], year 3: construction began on a new palace; the emperor moved into the Prince of Kuaiji residence.
translations.idiomatic: New palace works forced him into the Kuaiji princely mansion.

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑，雷雨，暴風，發屋折木。

translations.literal: Third month, yichou day [Apr 25]: thunder and rain; violent wind lifted roofs and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: Spring storms tore through the capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，大水。

translations.literal: Sixth month: great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Summer floods inundated lowlands.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛巳，帝入新宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, xinsi day [Aug 21]: the emperor entered the new palace.
translations.idiomatic: He took up residence in the finished halls.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，老人星見南方。

translations.literal: Yiyou day [Aug 25]: the Old Man star appeared in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Man star shone in the southern sky.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月辛酉，大赦，郡縣遭水旱者減租稅。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, xinyou day [Feb 17, 379 CE]: great amnesty; commanderies hit by flood or drought had rent and tax reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty paired with tax cuts for disaster counties.

sentences.zh: 丙子，謁建平等七陵。

translations.literal: Bingzi day [Mar 4]: visited seven tombs including Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed at seven tombs from Jianping onward.

sentences.zh: 二月戊午，苻堅使其子丕攻陷襄陽，執南中郎將朱序。

translations.literal: Second month, wuwu day [Apr 24]: Fu Jian’s son Fu Pi attacked and took Xiangyang, seizing General of the Gentlemen of the South of the Center Zhu Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi’s siege captured Zhu Xu and broke Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 又陷順陽。

translations.literal: He also took Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shunyang fell next.

sentences.zh: 三月，大疫。

translations.literal: Third month: great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Spring plague swept the realm.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔曰：「狡寇縱逸，籓守傾沒，疆埸之虞，事兼平日。

translations.literal: Renxu day [May 12]: an edict stated: “The crafty foe roams unchecked; screen defenses have fallen; border alarms exceed ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that frontier collapse demanded extraordinary effort.

sentences.zh: 其內外衆官，各悉心戮力，以康庶事。

translations.literal: Let civil and military officials inside and outside each devote heart and strength to bring peace to the myriad tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer was to rally to restore stability.

sentences.zh: 又年穀不登，百姓多匱。

translations.literal: Moreover the years grain did not ripen; the hundred surnames were largely destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Crop failure deepened popular want.

sentences.zh: 其詔御所供，事從儉約，九親供給，衆官廩俸，權可減半。

translations.literal: Therefore let palace supplies follow austerity; stipends for nine degrees of kin and salaries for the host of officials may provisionally be halved.
translations.idiomatic: Court consumption and official salaries faced a fifty-percent cut.

sentences.zh: 凡諸役費，自非軍國事要，皆宜停省，以周時務。

translations.literal: All labor expenses—unless essential to army and state—should stop and be curtailed to aid current priorities.
translations.idiomatic: Nonessential projects ended to free resources for crisis.

sentences.zh: 」癸未，使右將軍毛武生帥師伐蜀。

translations.literal: Guiwei day [Jun 12, 380 CE]: ordered General of the Right Mao Wusheng to lead troops and campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Mao Wusheng westward against Shu.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，苻堅將韋鐘陷魏興，太守吉挹死之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Fu Jian’s Wei Zhong took Weixing; Prefect Ji Yi died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin seized Weixing; Prefect Ji Yi fell defending it.

sentences.zh: 五月，苻堅將句難、彭超陷盱眙、高密內史毛璪之爲賊所執。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Fu Jian’s Ju Nan and Peng Chao took Xuyi; Interior Steward of Gaomi Mao Zhi was seized by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qin columns captured Xuyi and took Mao Zhi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 六月，大旱。

translations.literal: Sixth month: severe drought.
translations.idiomatic: Midsummer drought struck again.

sentences.zh: 戊子，征虜將軍謝玄及超、難戰于君川，大破之。

translations.literal: Wuzi day [Jul 17]: General Who Defeats Barbarians Xie Xuan engaged Chao and Nan at Jun River and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan shattered Ju Nan and Peng Chao at Junchuan.

sentences.zh: 秋八月丁亥，以左將軍王蘊爲尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, dinghai day [Sep 13]: General of the Left Wang Yun was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun became vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乙未，暴風，揚沙石。

translations.literal: Yiwei day [Sep 21]: violent wind drove sand and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Gales whipped grit through the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，盜殺安太守傅湛。

translations.literal: Ninth month: bandits killed Prefect Fu Zhan of Nan’an.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders murdered Nan’an Prefect Fu Zhan.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月己酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, jiyou day [Dec 27], new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: A winter new moon brought eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月乙巳，謁崇平陵。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, yisi day [Feb 11, 381 CE]: [the emperor] visited Chongping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed at Emperor Kang’s Chongping tomb.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，大旱。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: severe drought.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-month drought scorched the south.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，大赦五歲刑以下。

translations.literal: Guiyou day [May 14]: great amnesty for sentences of five years hard labor and below.
translations.idiomatic: Minor criminals up to five-year terms won release.

sentences.zh: 五月，大水。

translations.literal: Fifth month: great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: May floods rose across the lowlands.

sentences.zh: 以司徒謝安爲衛將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Xie An was made General Who Guards the Army with honor equal to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An kept education rank while adding guard-general parity with the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 六月甲寅，震含章殿四柱，並殺內侍二人。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jiayin day [Jul 18]: lightning struck the four pillars of Hanzhang Hall and killed two inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder shattered Hanzhang columns and killed two eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以比歲荒儉，大赦，自太元三年以前逋租宿債皆蠲除之，其鰥寡窮獨孤老不能自存者，人賜米五斛。

translations.literal: Jiazi day [Jul 28]: because successive years were famine-pinched, a great amnesty was issued; delinquent rent and old debts from before Taiyuan 3 were all remitted; widowers, widows, destitute, orphaned, and aged unable to support themselves each received five hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Famine amnesty wiped arrears through Taiyuan 3 and fed the helpless.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以驃騎將軍、琅邪王道子爲司徒。

translations.literal: Dingmao day [Jul 31]: General Who Inspires Might, Prince of Langye Daozi, became Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozi of Langye took the education portfolio.

sentences.zh: 秋九月癸未，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month, guiwei day [Oct 4]: Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang passed away.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，九真太守李遜據交州反。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Jiuzhen Prefect Li Xun seized Jiaozhou and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun carved out Jiaozhou from the far south.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙酉，葬定皇后于隆平陵。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, yiyou day [Dec 16]: Empress Ding was buried at Longping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She joined her tomb at Longping.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月，帝初奉佛法，立精舍於殿內，引諸沙門以居之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month of year 6 [382 CE]: the emperor first embraced Buddhism; he established a monastery chamber inside the palace hall and brought in monks to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: He opened palace chapels and lodged clerics within the walls.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以尚書謝石爲尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Dingyou day [Feb 16]: Director Xie Shi became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shi stepped up as vice director.

sentences.zh: 初置督運御史官。

translations.literal: For the first time the post of transport-censor was established.
translations.idiomatic: Transport inspectors oversaw grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 夏六月庚子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, gengzi day [Jul 7], new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Summer’s new moon eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 揚、荊、江三州大水。

translations.literal: Yang, Jing, and Jiang provinces suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangzi corridor flooded.

sentences.zh: 己巳，改制度，減煩費，損吏士員七百人。

translations.literal: Jisi day [Aug 6]: institutions were reformed, vexing expenses cut, and seven hundred clerk and soldier posts eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucracy shrank by seven hundred slots.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙子，赦五歲刑已下。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, bingzi day [Aug 13]: amnesty for sentences up to five years.
translations.idiomatic: Another round released lighter criminals.

sentences.zh: 甲午，交阯太守杜瑗斬李遜，交州平。

translations.literal: Jiawu day [Aug 31]: Jiaozhi Prefect Du Yuan beheaded Li Xun; Jiaozhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuan’s sword ended Li Xun’s revolt.

sentences.zh: 大饑。

translations.literal: Great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation gripped the countryside.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月己亥，以鎮軍大將軍郗愔爲司空。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, jihai day [Dec 24]: Grand General Who Guards the Army Xi Yin became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin traded army command for the works ministry.

sentences.zh: 會稽人檀元之反，自號安東將軍，鎮軍參軍謝藹之討平之。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji man Tan Yuanzhi rebelled, styling himself General Who Pacifies the East; Army Adviser Xie Aizhi attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yuanzhi’s eastern-sea bid collapsed before Xie Aizhi.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲辰，苻堅遣其襄陽太守閻震寇竟陵，襄陽太守桓石虔討擒之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, jiachen day [Jan 22, 383 CE]: Fu Jian sent his Xiangyang prefect Yan Zhen to raid Jingling; Xiangyang prefect Huan Shiqian attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shiqian bagged Yan Zhen’s raid on Jingling.

sentences.zh: 七年春三月，林邑范熊遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: Spring, third month of year 7 [383 CE]: Fan Xiong of Linyi sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Champa’s ruler offered gifts again.

sentences.zh: 秋八月癸卯，大赦。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, guimao day [Sep 21]: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn brought blanket pardon.

sentences.zh: 九月，東夷五國遣使來貢方物。

translations.literal: Ninth month: five eastern barbarian states sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Five Wa kingdoms dispatched tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將都貴焚燒沔北田穀，略襄陽百姓而去。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s Du Gui burned the grain fields north of the Han River and carried off Xiangyang commoners before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin raiders torched Hannan crops and dragged off civilians.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙子，雷。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, bingzi day [Nov 22]: thunder sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder rolled in winter—an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 八年春二月癸未，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, guiwei day [Mar 17, 384 CE]: yellow fog blocked all four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Sulfurous mist blanketed the horizon.

sentences.zh: 三月，始興、南康、廬陵大水，平地五丈。

translations.literal: Third month: Shixing, Nankang, and Luling suffered floods five fathoms deep on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Jiangxi drowned under thirty feet of water.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，大赦。

translations.literal: Dingsi day [Apr 28]: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Another empire-wide amnesty followed the floods.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，輔國將軍楊亮伐蜀，拔五城，擒苻堅將魏光。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: General Who Supports the State Yang Liang campaigned against Shu, took five towns, and captured Fu Jian’s Wei Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang clawed back Shu footholds and seized Wei Guang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，鷹揚將軍郭洽及苻堅將張崇戰于武當，大敗之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: General Who Spreads Might Guo Qia engaged Fu Jian’s Zhang Chong at Wudang and crushed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qia broke Zhang Chong on the Wudang road.

sentences.zh: 八月，苻堅帥衆渡淮，遣征討都督謝石、冠軍將軍謝玄、輔國將軍謝琰、西中郎將桓伊等距之。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Fu Jian led his host across the Huai; he dispatched Pacification Commander-in-Chief Xie Shi, Champion General Xie Xuan, General Who Supports the State Xie Yan, General of the Gentlemen of the West of the Center Huan Yi, and others to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Facing Fu Jian’s crossing, Jin threw Xie Shi, Xie Xuan, Xie Yan, and Huan Yi into the line.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔司徒、琅邪王道子錄尚書六條事。

translations.literal: Ninth month: an edict ordered Minister of Education and Prince of Langye Daozi recorder of affairs for the six statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozi joined the central recorder’s bench.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，苻堅弟融陷壽春。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Fu Jian’s younger brother Fu Rong took Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong seized Shouchun for the invasion.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，諸將及苻堅戰于肥水，大破之，俘斬數萬計，獲堅輿輦及雲母車。

translations.literal: Yihai day [Nov 18]: the various generals fought Fu Jian at the Fei River and smashed him; prisoners and heads numbered in the tens of thousands; Fu Jian’s palanquin and mica carriage were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Feishui broke Former Qin’s host and captured Fu Jian’s conveyances.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚申，詔衛將軍謝安勞旋師于金城。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, gengshen day [Dec 12]: an edict ordered General Who Guards the Army Xie An to feast the returning army at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An welcomed the victors at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 壬子，立陳留王世子靈誕爲陳留王。

translations.literal: Renzi day [Dec 4]: Sun Bao, heir apparent of Prince of Chenliu, was established Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenliu heir Sun Bao succeeded to his princely title.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚午，以寇難初平，大赦。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, gengwu day [Jan 22, 385 CE]: because the bandit peril had just been pacified, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Feishui amnesty marked restored calm.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍謝石爲尚書令。

translations.literal: General of the Central Army Xie Shi was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shi took the secretariat’s head chair.

sentences.zh: 開酒禁。

translations.literal: The prohibition on brewing was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Wine bans ended in celebration.

sentences.zh: 始增百姓稅米，口五石。

translations.literal: For the first time commoners’ grain tax was increased to five shi per person.
translations.idiomatic: The rice levy jumped to five shi per capita.

sentences.zh: 前句町王翟遼背苻堅，舉兵於河南，慕容垂自鄴與遼合，遂攻堅子暉於洛陽。

translations.literal: The former king of Juding, Di Liao, broke with Fu Jian and raised troops in Henan; Murong Chui came from Ye to join Liao, then attacked Fu Jian’s son Hui at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao’s Henan revolt drew Murong Chui; together they pressed Fu Hui at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 仇池公楊世奔還隴右，遣使稱籓。

translations.literal: Duke of Chouchi Yang Shi fled back to Longyou and sent envoys declaring submission.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi rushed west and renewed fealty to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 九年春正月庚子，封武陵王孫寶爲臨川王。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, gengzi day [Feb 16, 385 CE]: Sun Bao, grandson of Prince of Wuling, was enfeoffed Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: A Wuling grandson, Sun Bao, received the Linchuan seat.

sentences.zh: 戊午，立新寧王晞子遵爲新寧王。

translations.literal: Wuwu day [Mar 6]: the son of Prince of Xinning Xi, Zun, was established Prince of Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinning princely seat passed to Zun.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，謁建平等四陵。

translations.literal: Xinhai day [Mar 9]: visited four tombs including Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed again at the western tombs.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉牢之克譙城。

translations.literal: General of Dragon Soaring Liu Laizhi took Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi seized Qiao from Qin holdouts.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍桓沖部將郭寶伐新城、魏興、上庸三郡，降之。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Huan Chong’s officer Guo Bao attacked the three commanderies Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong and brought them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Bao folded the Han River triple cities.

sentences.zh: 二月辛巳，使持節、都督荊江梁寧益交廣七州諸軍事、車騎將軍、荊州刺史桓沖卒。

translations.literal: Second month, xinsi day [Mar 29]: Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, commander-in-chief of Jing, Jiang, Liang, Ning, Yi, Jiao, and Guang military affairs, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Jingzhou Inspector Huan Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong died holding the lower Yangzi theater.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂自洛陽與翟遼攻苻堅子丕於鄴。

translations.literal: Murong Chui from Luoyang with Zhai Liao attacked Fu Pi (Fu Jian’s son) at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui and Zhai Liao closed on Ye against Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 三月，以衛將軍謝安爲太保。

translations.literal: Third month: General Who Guards the Army Xie An became Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An moved to grand mentor with honors.

sentences.zh: 苻堅北地長史慕容泓、平陽太守慕容沖並起兵背堅。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s Northern Di Chief Clerk Murong Hong and Pingyang Prefect Murong Chong both raised troops and turned against Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Murong brothers rose in Guanzhong against Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己卯，增置太學生百人。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, jimao day [May 15]: one hundred more Imperial University students were added.
translations.idiomatic: The state academy grew by a hundred places.

sentences.zh: 封張天錫爲西平公。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxi was enfeoffed Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: The fallen Liang ruler kept rank as Xiping duke.

sentences.zh: 使竟陵太守趙統伐襄陽，克之。

translations.literal: Ordered Jingling Prefect Zhao Tong to campaign against Xiangyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tong reclaimed Xiangyang for Jin.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將姚萇背堅，起兵於北地，自立爲王，國號秦。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s Yao Chang rebelled against Jian, raised troops in Northern Di, styled himself king, with dynastic title Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang broke away and founded Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑朔，崇德皇太后褚氏崩。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guichou day [Jul 12], new moon: Empress Dowager Chongde, Lady Chu, died.
translations.idiomatic: Regent empress dowager Chu died.

sentences.zh: 慕容泓爲其叔父沖所殺，沖自稱皇太弟。

translations.literal: Murong Hong was killed by his uncle Chong; Chong styled himself imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong murdered Hong and claimed Yan heir status.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊戌，遣兼司空、高密王純之修謁洛陽五陵。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, wuxu day [Aug 17]: concurrently Minister of Works, Prince of Gaomi Chunzhi was sent to repair sacrifice at the five Luoyang tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhi swept the lost northern imperial graves.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬康獻皇后于崇平陵。

translations.literal: Jiyou day [Aug 28]: Empress Kangxian was buried at Chongping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chu joined Chongping beside her consort.

sentences.zh: 百濟遣使來貢方物。

translations.literal: Baekje sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje offered southern seas gifts.

sentences.zh: 苻堅及慕容沖戰于鄭西，堅師敗績。

translations.literal: Fu Jian and Murong Chong fought west of Ye; Jian’s army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong shattered Fu Jian west of the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 八月戊寅，司空郗愔薨。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuyin day [Sep 26]: Minister of Works Xi Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin died in office.

sentences.zh: 九月辛卯，前鋒都督謝玄攻苻堅將兗州刺史張崇于鄄城，克之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, xinmao day [Oct 11]: Vanguard Commander-in-Chief Xie Xuan attacked Fu Jian’s Yanzhou Inspector Zhang Chong at Juancheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan drove Zhang Chong from Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 甲午，加太保謝安大都督揚、江、荊、司、豫、徐、兗、青、冀、幽、幷、梁、益、雍、涼十五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Jiawu day [Oct 14]: Grand Mentor Xie An was added commander-in-chief of military affairs for Yang, Jiang, Jing, Si, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Bing, Liang, Yi, Yong, and Liang—fifteen provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An assumed sweeping theater command over fifteen provinces.

sentences.zh: 十二月，苻堅將呂光稱制于河右，自號酒泉公。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Fu Jian’s Lü Guang assumed regency west of the River and styled himself Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang carved out the northwest as his own.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖僭卽皇帝位于阿房。

translations.literal: Murong Chong usurped the imperial title at Epang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong crowned himself at Epang Palace.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月甲午，謁諸陵。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, jiawu day [Feb 25, 386 CE]: visited the various tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Spring sacrifices swept the mausoleum row.

sentences.zh: 二月，立國學。

translations.literal: Second month: established the National University.
translations.idiomatic: A state academy opened at the capital.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡太守任權斬苻堅益州刺史李平，益州平。

translations.literal: Shu Prefect Ren Quan beheaded Fu Jian’s Yizhou Inspector Li Ping; Yizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Quan’s coup cleared Shu of Qin officers.

sentences.zh: 三月，滎陽人鄭燮以郡來降。

translations.literal: Third month: the Xingyang man Zheng Xie brought his commandery to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyang flipped to Jin.

sentences.zh: 苻堅國亂，使使奉表請迎。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s state was in turmoil; he sent envoys presenting a memorial requesting escort.
translations.idiomatic: The beaten Fu Jian begged Jin for rescue.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉牢之及慕容垂戰于黎陽，王師敗績。

translations.literal: General of Dragon Soaring Liu Laizhi fought Murong Chui at Liyang; the royal army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi lost to Murong Chui on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙辰，劉牢之與沛郡太守周次及垂戰于五橋澤，王師又敗績。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, bingchen day [May 21]: Liu Laizhi with Pei Prefect Zhou Ci fought Chui at Five Bridges Marsh; the royal army was again routed.
translations.idiomatic: Second defeat followed at Five Bridges Marsh.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，太保謝安帥衆救苻堅。

translations.literal: Renxu day [May 27]: Grand Mentor Xie An led troops to rescue Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An marched ostensibly to aid the stranded Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 五月，大水。

translations.literal: Fifth month: great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Late spring floods returned.

sentences.zh: 苻堅留太子宏守長安，奔于五將山。

translations.literal: Fu Jian left Crown Prince Hong to guard Chang’an and fled to Five Generals Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian abandoned Chang’an for the hills.

sentences.zh: 六月，宏來降，慕容沖入長安。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Hong came to surrender; Murong Chong entered Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince capitulated as Yan forces took the Wei valley capital.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，苻丕自枋頭西走，龍驤將軍檀玄追之，爲丕所敗。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Fu Pi fled west from Fangtou; General of Dragon Soaring Tan Xuan pursued him and was defeated by Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi outran Tan Xuan’s pursuit from Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 旱，饑。

translations.literal: Drought; famine.
translations.idiomatic: Parched fields brought hunger again.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，老人星見。

translations.literal: Dingsi day [Aug 24]: the Old Man star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Man star rose—auspice of age.

sentences.zh: 九月，呂光據姑臧，自稱涼州刺史。

translations.literal: September: Lü Guang seized Guzang and styled himself Liangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang seized Wuwei and claimed Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻丕僭卽皇帝位于晉陽。

translations.literal: Fu Pi usurped the imperial title at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi declared emperor from Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁亥，論淮肥之功，追封謝安廬陵郡公，封謝石南康公，謝玄康樂公，謝琰望蔡公，桓伊永脩公，自餘封拜各有差。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, dinghai day [Nov 22]: rewards for the Huai-Fei merit—posthumously enfeoff Xie An Duke of Luling commandery, Xie Shi Duke of Nankang, Xie Xuan Duke of Kangle, Xie Yan Duke of Wangcai, Huan Yi Duke of Yongxiu; remaining enfeoffments differed by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Feishui heroes received ducal stacks—Xie kin and Huan Yi foremost.

sentences.zh: 是歲，乞伏國仁自稱大單于、秦河二州牧。

translations.literal: That year Qifu Guoren styled himself Grand Chanyu and shepherd of Qin and He provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin’s Qifu Guoren proclaimed dual shepherdships.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月辛未，慕容垂僭卽皇帝位于中山。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, xinwei day [Feb 15, 387 CE]: Murong Chui usurped the imperial title at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan rose with Murong Chui’s throne at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 壬午，翟遼襲黎陽，執太守滕恬之。

translations.literal: Renwu day [Feb 26]: Zhai Liao raided Liyang and seized Prefect Teng Tianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao snatched Liyang and captured Teng Tianzhi.

sentences.zh: 乙酉。

translations.literal: Yiyou day [Feb 29].
translations.idiomatic: The chronicle marks yiyou.

sentences.zh: 謁諸陵。

translations.literal: Visited the various tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He ended the season at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖將許木末殺慕容沖于長安。

translations.literal: Murong Chong’s general Xu Mumou killed Murong Chong in Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: A Yan officer murdered Murong Chong inside the fallen western capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，大赦。

translations.literal: Third month: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Spring brought another blanket pardon.

sentences.zh: 太山太守張願以郡叛，降于翟遼。

translations.literal: Taishan Prefect Zhang Yuan rebelled with his commandery and surrendered to Zhai Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan flipped to Zhai Liao’s coalition.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，以百濟王世子餘暉爲使持節、都督、鎮東將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Baekje crown prince Yu Hui was appointed Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, commander-in-chief, General Who Guards the East, and king of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje’s heir received Jin investiture and full general’s regalia.

sentences.zh: 代王拓拔圭始改稱魏。

translations.literal: King of Dai Tuoba Gui first changed his state title to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuoba ruler began calling his realm Wei.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以尚書僕射陸納爲尚書左僕射，譙王恬爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Guisi day [May 4]: Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Na became Left Vice Director; Prince of Qiao Tian became Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na and Prince Tian split the secretariat’s two chairs.

sentences.zh: 六月己卯，地震。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jimao day [Jul 3]: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tremors returned.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以前輔國將軍楊亮爲西戎校尉、雍州刺史，鎮衛山陵。

translations.literal: Gengyin day [Jul 14]: former General Who Supports the State Yang Liang became Colonel of the Western Rong and Yongzhou inspector, guarding the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang was posted to guard the Guanzhong mausolea.

sentences.zh: 秋八月庚午，封孔靖之爲奉聖亭侯，奉宣尼祀。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, gengwu day [Sep 2]: Kong Jingzhi was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengsheng village to tend Master Xuan’s sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A Confucius caretaker received a hereditary fief for the sage’s cult.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，安平王邃之薨。

translations.literal: Dinghai day [Sep 19]: Prince of Anping Suizhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Anping passed away.

sentences.zh: 翟遼寇譙，龍驤將軍朱序擊走之。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao raided Qiao; General of Dragon Soaring Zhu Xu struck him back.
